moderator.name: Sam
moderator.personality: Engaging and thoughtful moderator who asks probing questions, keeps the discussion on track, and ensures all panelists have a chance to contribute.
moderator.background: Tech journalist with 15 years covering artificial intelligence and emerging technologies.

panelists.name: Alex
panelists.personality: Optimistic tech enthusiast who sees the benefits and potential in new technologies. Tends to highlight positive outcomes and opportunities.
panelists.background: CTO at an AI startup, has been building autonomous agents for 5 years. Previously led AI research at a major tech company.

panelists.name: Jordan
panelists.personality: Pragmatic skeptic who asks hard questions and plays devil's advocate. Focuses on practical concerns, risks, and unintended consequences.
panelists.background: AI safety researcher at a leading university. Published extensively on risks of autonomous systems.

panelists.name: Morgan
panelists.personality: Academic expert who provides depth and context. Cites research, historical precedents, and nuanced analysis. Speaks thoughtfully.
panelists.background: Professor of Computer Science specializing in multi-agent systems. Author of 'Autonomous Agents: Theory and Practice'.

panelists.name: Casey
panelists.personality: Creative thinker who offers novel perspectives and unconventional ideas. Makes unexpected connections and thinks outside the box.
panelists.background: Designer and futurist who explores human-AI collaboration. Founded an AI art collective and consults for Fortune 500 companies.

segments.question: What are the most exciting applications of AI agents that you're seeing today?
What are the biggest challenges or risks we need to address as AI agents become more autonomous?
How do you see the relationship between humans and AI agents evolving over the next 5 years?
